1.menu: Berkshire K loseu gaseu (Berkshire K pork sirloin cutlet), loseu gaseu (pork sirloin cutlet), katsu sando (pork cutlet sandwich), modum gaseu (assorted cutlets), ebi gaseu (prawn cutlet)
1.desc: This restaurant serves Japanese-style tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet). They make their tonkatsu to order, frying it first at a low temperature, then at a high temperature, and allowing it proper resting time before serving, resulting in meat that is tender, pink, and juicy. Eating it with Maldon salt, the royal salt of the UK, or adding mustard to the special sauce, reduces the greasiness.

2.menu: kani (crab), beomgodong saenggang jorim (braised sea snail with ginger), sashimi (sliced raw fish), buri sio tataki (salted chopped yellowtail), hanu kushiage (deep-fried korean beef skewers), kamotsuke somyeon (cold buckwheat noodles dipped in warm duck broth), chamdom ochazuke (sea bream ochazuke), fugu zosui (pufferfish rice soup)
2.desc: Led by Chef Myung Jung-hyo, a pioneering figure in Busan’s Japanese culinary scene, the kaiseki restaurant Juga Jung-hyo makes its long-awaited return. The restaurant presents a sake-focused, appetizer-driven course designed to maximize harmony with carefully selected sake, with the menu evolving approximately every month to reflect the flow of the seasons. A signature dish of chilled somen noodles generously infused with freshly ground sesame seeds stands as a defining highlight of the experience.

3.menu: espresso, Americano, caffe latte, flat white, vanilla latte, einspanner, filter coffee, apple and cinnamon ade, apple cinnamon black tea, cupcake (carrot / lemon / blueberry / black tea)
3.desc: This coffee shop is a rising star in the specialty coffee boom in Jeonpo-dong. They first opened in the Suyeong area but recently relocated to Jeonpo-dong. This light-roasting coffee shop, along with others like Mesh and Deep Blue Lake, has come to represent Korean coffee. They roast distinctive green coffee beans with clear fruity and floral aromas, and even coffees with a fascinating balance and sweetness are wellrepresented.

4.menu: hand-drip coffee, espresso, Americano, yuginong milk tea (organic milk tea), Victoria ttalgi cake (Victoria strawberry cake), malcha chocolat cake (matcha chocolat cake), basil cheese scone, vanilla madeleine, cherry financier
4.desc: Along with Momos, this specialty coffee company has come to represent Busan. They operate eight large coffee shops in Busan, Ulsan, and Gyeongnam. The most representative location is the first Blackup coffee shop in Seomyeon, which established Busan's Seomyeon Café Street. Their Blend Coffee Nero has been consistently popular for over ten years. Another favorite is their creative sea salt coffee, which combines cold brew coffee and fresh cream with a pinch of sea salt.

5.menu: espresso, Americano filter coffee, caffe latte, cold brew, earl grey, bagel
5.desc: Along with Heate, this coffee shop is one of the leaders of the recent specialty-coffee wave in Busan. Coffee roasting, store management, planning, events, and creative activities are popular not only in Busan but also nationwide. The monastery-like store was so popular in the early days that numerous imitation stores appeared nationwide, but after the renovation, the atmosphere became more focused on the coffee itself.

6.menu: hand-drip coffee of the day, Americano, espresso, kangkang (iced coffee with kumquat sherbet), cold brew, caffe latte, seasonal tea, lemon pound cake, croissant, cream brownie, cheese cake
6.desc: This coffee shop opened in 2007 as a small takeout store near Oncheonjang Station. One of the founders, barista Jeon Joo-yeon, is the first Korean barista to win two consecutive World Barista Championships. The coffee shop, designed in the style of an old jeoksan gaok (Japanese colonial house), is beautiful, and they recently opened a large-scale roastery and second store in Yeongdo. The signature coffees are their Es Chocolat blend and Fruity Bonbon blend. The coffee shop was also the first in Korea to introduce many coffees from such sources as the Savage Coffee auction in Panama.

7.menu: Hagwonjeon (sponge cake), chamchi ppang (stuffed tuna bread), jayeonhyomo ppang (sourdough bread), myeongnan baguette (pollack roe baguette), honey cream cheese, danggeun cake (carrot cake), brioche roll, sogeum ppang (salted butter roll), mascarpone pudding
7.desc: This bakery is one of the most popular in Busan and is known for its large, soft, and non-greasy choux cream puffs. Their choux cream puff bread is also gaining popularity and can sell out quickly, so you need to hurry

8.menu: Brilliant collection, Brillant grand boîte, madeleine, financier, canelé, gâteaux au citron, galette bretonne, santtalgi hateusyu (raspberry chou)
8.desc: This bakery specializes in baked confectioneries and serves traditional French sweets. Pre-ordering is required one day in advance, as they operate primarily with pre-orders and sell out quickly.

9.menu: croissant, ciabatta, basil meongmul baguette (basil & squid ink baguette), bam sikppang (chestnut loaf bread), tongmil sikppang (whole wheat bread), ttalgi pastry (strawberry pastry), jambon sandwich
9.desc: This bakery offers a variety of baked goods. Their various kinds of baguettes are popular. Their delicately layered croissants and plain bread are also delicious.

10.menu: Mont Blanc cake, bûchette, forêt blanche, fraisier, poire caramel (caramel pear cake), canelé, jeorinbae clafouti (clafouti aux poires), caffe allongé, caffe latte, tea
10.desc: This dessert café is known for its sweet bread, baked goods, and cakes. They also serve a variety of teas to accompany the desserts. Some of their most popular items include the Mont Blanc and forêt blanche

11.menu: baton, baguette, oat almond, pain au chocolat, croissant, cinnamon roll, olives
11.desc: This French-style bakery cafe uses French ingredients, like flour, salt, butter, and chocolate. Their most popular bread is the stick-shaped baton, and a maximum of five can be purchased per person.

12.menu: Americano, caffe latte, sainthonoré, pistachio Paris-brest , lavender mousse tart with Marco Polo ganache and raspberry, raspberry saint-honoré, masion chocolat éclair
12.desc: This is a place where you can indulge in luxuriously plated desserts. The light purple lavender mousse topped with violets is a popular item, and the raspberry jam pairs perfectly with the tart pastry.

13.menu: ttalgi mille-feuille (strawberry mille-feuille), tarte chocolat, orange cocoa madeleine, muhwagwa keurimchijeu financier (fig butter cream cheese financier), Haenam bamgoguma crème brulée (sweet potato crème brulée), Americano, caffe latte
13.desc: This place specializes in traditional French pastries, such as madeleines and financiers. The chocolate tarts, which are rich in chocolate, and the millefeuilles are among the most popular menu items. They also have seasonal items, such as strawberry mille-feuilles and chestnut madeleines.

14.menu: hanu saenggalbi (grilled Korean beef galbi), hanu yangnyeom galbi (grilled marinated Korean galbi), bulgogi, ttukbaegi doenjang (soybean paste jjigae hot pot)
14.desc: This restaurant is considered the birthplace of Haeundae-style ribs. Since opening in 1964, it has maintained its reputation for quality. After grilling the meat on the special grill pan shaped like a jeongol (hotpot) pan, you can order potato noodles to add and enjoy it like a hotpot. Because the restaurant is in a hanok (traditional Korean house), you feel like a guest in a nobleman's house. Many celebrities are frequent customers

15.menu: jaecheop guk (marsh clam soup), jaecheop hoe (raw marsh clams)
15.desc: This is the original restaurant in Samnakdong's "Jaecheop Alley." Along with an order of jaecheopguk (small clam soup), they serve rice, a large bowl for mixing, braised mackerel, kkakdugi (radish kimchi), kimchi, and doenjang-jjigae (soybean paste stew). The rice mixed with the jaecheop and seasoning goes perfectly with the refreshing soup. The reason their rice tastes so good is that they make their rice in a cast-iron pot.

16.menu: suyuk (boiled pork slices), guksu (noodles), yeolmu guksu (young summer radish kimchi noodles)
16.desc: This restaurant specializes in dwaeji-suyuk (boiled pork) and has a 100-year history. The suyuk is served in generous portions. The dwaeji-sagolguksu (pork bone noodle soup) they serve as a meal is a reliable option. Suyuk can also be purchased to take home.

17.menu: bok guk (puffer fish soup), bok bulgogi (puffer fish bulgogi), bok course (pufferfish full-course set menu)
17.desc: This restaurant is renowned for its pufferfish cuisine and has been handed down for two generations over the past 60 years. You can choose from a variety of pufferfish dishes, such as bokchiri (clear pufferfish soup) and bok-maeuntang (spicy pufferfish soup), and you can choose the pufferfish you want. When you order a pufferfish full course set menu, you will be served pufferfish prepared a variety of ways: as shabu-shabu, deep-fried, in a sweet-and-sour salad, and as a porridge. It is so popular that there are branches all over Busan.

18.menu: nakji bokkeum (spicy stir-fried octopus), nakji saeu bokkeum (spicy stir-fried shrimp and octopus), nakji sogopchang bokkeum (spicy stir-fried beef intestines and octopus), nakji saeu sogopchang bokkeum (spicy stir-fried Shrimp, beef intestines, and octopus, sari (side order)
18.desc: This restaurant has been serving nakji-bokkeum (stir-fried octopus) for over 50 years. This is nakjibokkeum, but their version contains broth, so it's more like jeongol (hot pot). The variation with beef small intestine is also recommended. The nakjibokkeum can be mixed with rice or boiled with udon noodles.

19.menu: teuk yang (ox tripe), daechang (grilled beef large intestines), gopchang (grilled beef small intestines / grilled pork small intestines), baekteugyang (grilled beef tripe special), yeomtong (grilled thinly-sliced beef heart), kongpat (beef kidneys)
19.desc: This restaurant specializes in yang (smooth tripe) and gopchang (small intestine) and has over 60 years of tradition. Korean beef smooth tripe and small intestines are marinated in homemade sesame oil and marinade, and then grilled over charcoal. The smooth tripe, and small and large intestines are all of high quality, and the seasoning complements the flavors perfectly. The seasoning sauce is Gyeongsang-do style, made by mixing red pepper powder and starch syrup. The smooth-tripe fried rice is also delicious.

20.menu: jjajangmyeon (noodles in black bean sauce), udon, jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup), tangsuyuk (deep-fried pork with sweet and sour sauce), kkanpunggi (sweet and spicychicken)
20.desc: This 70-year-old restaurant specializes in Sichuan Chinese cuisine. Popular menu items include the jajang-myeon (noodles and Sichuan sauce with a fiery, smoky flavor) and classic tangsuyuk (sweet-and-sour beef or pork) with large chunks of cucumber, carrots, and jelly ear mushrooms. In addition, they serve delicious kkanpunggi (spicy garlic fried chicken).

21.menu: This place serves dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice), which has a refreshing and savory flavor. It also serves well-cooked suyuk (steamed pork) and sundae (Korean sausage) in generous portions. This place is located in Nampo-dong International Market and has become a popular tourist destination in Busan because of its delicious food.
21.desc: This place serves dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice), which has a refreshing and savory flavor. It also serves well-cooked suyuk (steamed pork) and sundae (Korean sausage) in generous portions. This place is located in Nampo-dong International Market and has become a popular tourist destination in Busan because of its delicious food.

22.menu: gogi mandu (meat mandu), jjin gyoja (steamed dumplings), gun mandu (pan-fried mandu), maepgun (spicy seasoned fried mandu), saeu gyoza (shrimp dumplings), mala mandu
22.desc: This restaurant is well-known for its Chinese dumplings, which have a thick yet soft skin and a well-balanced filling of ginger and pork. In addition to Chinese dumplings, they also specialize in Chinese breads such as pat-bbang (red-bean bread) and dalgyal-bbang (egg bread). Bean soup, which is a popular breakfast food in China, is served with snacks. This restaurant has a history of over 70 years.

23.menu: dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), sundae gukbap (sundae and rice soup), naejang gukbap (offal and rice soup), ttaro gukbap (rice and soup), suyuk baekban (boiled pork slices set menu), chapssal sundae (sweet rice sundae), suyuk (boiled pork slices)
23.desc: This restaurant's dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice) is made from the best cuts of pork and is milky and clean-tasting. Another popular item is their chapssal-sundae (Korean sausage), which is made with glutinous rice instead of cellophane noodles. They have been in business for 80 years and are one of the original restaurants in Seomyeon's "dwaeji-gukbap Alley.

24.menu: seolleongtang (ox bone soup), gomtang (beef bone soup), yangjitang (brisket and flank soup), suyuk (boiled pork slices)
24.desc: This restaurant has been serving seolleongtang (ox-bone soup) for over eighty years. Seolleongtang is a popular dish in Seoul, but it has also won over the taste buds of Busan residents. The restaurant only serves two side dishes, kimchi and kkakdugi (radish kimchi), but the flavor is excellent.

25.menu: yukhoe bibimbap (beef tartare bibimbap), dolsot bibimbap (hot stone pot bibimbap), hoe bibimbap (raw fish bibimbap), seoksoe bulgogi (grilled bulgogi), yukhoe (beef tartare), gaori muchim (spicy ray salad), pajeon (green onion pancake)
25.desc: This 70-year-old restaurant serves Jinju-style yukhoe bibimbap, a dish made with fresh raw beef and various vegetables that are evenly mixed together. When you order the bibimbap, they also serve seonjitguk (hangover soup with oxblood) and mul kimchi (water kimchi), which are delicacies. Other menu items include grilled bulgogi, pajeon (green-onion pancakes), and gaori-muchim (seasoned raw stingray).

26.menu: Busanae ppang (bread with sweet potato and cream cheese filling), croissant, French pie, mini castella, sangtu gwaja (white bean paste cookies), choco muffin, cheese muffin, pain de gênes, Mont Blanc bread, soboru ppang (Korean streusel bun), ttalgi saengkeurim mini cake (strawberry mini cake with whipped cream)
26.desc: This old bakery in Busan has been in business for over 40 years. Their popular menu items include the salad bun with potato-salad filling and pie manju. In addition to traditional breads, they also offer Mont Blancs and egg tarts.

27.menu: hoe baekban (sliced raw fish set menu), hoe bibimbap (raw fish bibimbap), mulhoe (cold raw fish soup), jeonbok juk (abalone rice porridge), dom meori tang (sea bream head stew), saengseon yangnyeomgui (grilled marinated fish head)
27.desc: This 80-year-old hoe-baekban-jip (sashimi restaurant) is located in Jagalchi Market. The generous portions of thick-cut sashimi, the chojang (sour and spicy dipping sauce), and the side dishes are all tantalizing. Their hoebaekban (sashimi set meal) comes with a plate of sashimi, rice, clear fish soup, and five or six side dishes. Depending on the season, salted fish intestines, salted rockfish, and crab sauce are also served.

28.menu: Baekgu pie (109-layered pastry with custard-cream filling), croizen (soft roll filled with corn salad), ssuk ssal sikppang (mugwort rice loaf bread), bluebarry sikppang (blueberry loaf bread), pat donut (donut with red bean filling), Italian croquette, chapssal pat donut (sweet rice red bean donut), baguette pizza, yachae ppang (vegetable bun), sausage pastry
28.desc: This bakery in Busan has been in operation for over 60 years. The most popular item is their croizen, a soft roll filled with corn salad. They also sell a variety of other simple but delicious oldfashioned kinds of bread that are popular with those who have fond memories of them.

29.menu: Dongnae samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup), gungjung yakgyetang (chicken soup with medicinal herbs)
29.desc: This restaurant specializes in samgyetang (chickenginseng soup) and has only two items on the menu: goong-joong yakgyetang (royal chicken soup with medicinal herbs) and Dongnae samgyetang. The soup is made with a large chicken, and the broth is rich and flavorful. A glass of ginseng wine is served before the soup, which is topped with green onions. The restaurant is popular and often has a long line of customers.

30.menu: bok guk (puffer fish soup), bok maeuntang (spicy puffer fish stew), eunbok suyuk (boiled brown-backed toadfish slices), daegutang (codfish soup)
30.desc: Here, you can enjoy clean-tasting bokguk (pufferfish soup). The key to making bokguk is to use enough meat and prepare a flavorful broth, and this restaurant is known for its delicious bokguk with a rich, concentrated broth. The restaurant is small but popular, so you may have to wait in line during lunchtime.

31.menu: agwi jjim (spicy braised monkfish), agwi suyuk (boiled monkfish slices), agwi tang (monkfish soup)
31.desc: This restaurant has been making agui-jjim (braised spicy monkfish) for over 60 years. They use only fresh monkfish, so their agui-jjim has a clean taste and a refreshing aftertaste. The scent and taste of their agui-jjim may be unfamiliar because it contains Korean mint leaves, which are eaten by people from Gyeongsang-do.

32.menu: Dongnae pajeon (Dongnae green onion pancake), Dongnae godong jjim (steamed sea snails), yakcho jeonbyeong muchim (medicinalherb buckwheat pancake and duck salad), samsaek deodeok gui (grilled deodeok root), golbaengi muchim (sea snail salad), Ttugisang (set menu), Ttumisang (set menu)
32.desc: This restaurant has been in business for over eighty years and has been passed down through four generations. It is famous for its pajeon, which is a thick green onion pancake that is hearty enough to be a meal on its own. The pajeon has a rich flavor and is made with a mixture of various seafood, including clams, shrimp, oysters, mussels, and other seafood and fried in rapeseed oil. The restaurant also offers a popular Korean table setting menu, which includes pajeon, braised godong-jjim (steamed seasoned turban shells), golbaengi-muchim (moon snail salad), and deodeok-gui (grilled lance asiabell root).

33.menu: gomjangeo (inshore hagfish (straw fire-grilled, grilled marinated, grilled whole, or salt-grilled)), gomjangeo maeuntang (spicy inshore hagfish stew), gomjangeo doenjangguk (inshore hagfish soybean paste soup)
33.desc: This restaurant is the originator of grilling Gijang gomjangeo (sea eel from Gijang) over a straw fire. After the sea eel has been moderately grilled over a straw fire, you can peel off the charred skin to reveal the golden brown flesh, which you can cut in bite-size pieces and dip in sesame oil or salt. You can have pine needle sea eel, which imparts an aromatic flavor, and sea eel doenjangguk (bean paste soup), which has a savory flavor.

34.menu: mul mandu (boiled mandu), jjin mandu (steamed mandu), gun mandu (pan-fried mandu), mandu gukbap (mandu rice soup)
34.desc: This is a place where you can enjoy handmade, oldfashioned steamed dumplings. It is run by an ethnic Chinese. The dumplings are made fresh daily, so they are juicy and flavorful. Fried dumplings are also a popular menu item, and mandu gukbap (dumpling soup and rice) is recommended for a full meal. You can feel the passion that has gone into making dumplings for over 50 years. Please note that fried dumplings are only available after 10:30 AM.

35.menu: bok guk (puffer fish soup), bok twigim (deep-fried puffer fish), bokkkeopjil twigim (fried puffer fish skin) , bok kkeopjil muchim (puffer fish skin salad), bok jjim (braised puffer fish), bok suyuk (boiled puffer fish slices), bok sashimi (sliced raw puffer fish)
35.desc: This is the oldest bokguk restaurant in the Haeundae area. Bokguk (pufferfish soup) is Busan's representative hangover soup, and a bowl of clear jiri bokguk completely cures a hangover. The spicy bokmaeuntang is also popular, but if you want to enjoy cleantasting pufferfish, the jiri bokguk is recommended. On the second floor, they offer a variety of pufferfish course set menus.

36.desc: This restaurant specializes in just one thing: myeolchi guksu (noodles in anchovy broth). When you order noodles, you will be served boiled noodles and a kettle of broth, and you can pour as much broth as you like over the noodles. The broth is prepared by simmering anchovies from the southern coast of Korea. It is best enjoyed with plenty of chopped Cheongyang peppers. This restaurant is considered to be the originator of Gupo noodles.

37.menu: mul milmyeon (cold wheat noodles) , bibim milmyeon (spicy wheat noodles), Gaegeum mandu , gogigomyeong (meat garnish), hoegomyeong chuga (extra sliced raw fish garnish)
37.desc: This restaurant has been serving milmyeon (wheat noodles) for over fifty years, making it one of the oldest milmyeon restaurants, along with Gaya Milmyeon. The noodles are made with a combination of wheat flour and sweet potato starch, which gives them their characteristic chewy texture. In the summer, expect to wait in line for a table.

38.menu: dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), naejang gukbap (offal and rice soup), guksu (noodles), ttaro gukbap (rice and soup), suybaek (boiled pork slices set menu), suyuk (boiled pork slices)
38.desc: This restaurant is famous for its Busan-style dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice) with Chinese chives. The soup is clear and refreshing, and the taste is enhanced by adding plenty of Chinese chives. 'Subaek' means suyuk-baekban, which is rice and pork soup with the boiled pork slices and sundae (Korean sausage) served on the side

39.menu: lunch set, dinner, first seating , dinner, second seating
39.desc: Here, they serve sushi omakase (chef's choice) made with fresh, high-quality seasonal ingredients. In the dinner course set menu, more than ten kinds of tsumami (Japanese hors d'oeuvres) are offered first. Served on a Dior plate, their signature dish is tuna, sea urchin, and avocado mousse, which is wrapped in laver before eating. They serve Mazuma wasabi that they bring in by air from Shizuoka and grate just before serving.

40.menu: lunch full-course set menu, dinner course
40.desc: This French restaurant claims to be a neobistro. From amuse-bouches to appetizers and main courses, the dishes are beautifully plated and made with high-quality ingredients. The restaurant started as a wine bar, so wine pairing is highly recommended.

41.menu: lunch full-course set menu, dinner course, bukgyeong ori (Peking duck), Ibérico chashu, basakhan samgyeopsal barbecue (crispy barbecued pork belly), jeonbog yangjangpi (abalone starch sheet salad with mustard sauce), buldojang (Buddha's temptation soup), sacheonsik laziji (Sichuan spicy chicken with eggplant), hunyeonhyang mero (smoked patagonian toothfish)
41.desc: This modern Chinese restaurant in the Grand Josun Busan hotel has a panoramic ocean view. Their Peking duck is definitely the standout dish, while chili shrimp with Shaoxing wine and smoked grouper are also popular choices. You can also enjoy signature dishes from Hongyeon in the Westin Josun, such as buldojang ('Buddha-JumpsOver-the-Wall' soup) and tangsuyuk (sweet and sour pork). The Peking duck must be ordered at least two days in advance.

42.menu: lunch set , dinner set, Chaoran's Peking duck, dim sum selection
42.desc: This is a Chinese restaurant located in the Signiel Hotel in Busan. They offer modern Cantonese cuisine in a setting inspired by 1920s Hong Kong. During the day, you can enjoy dim sum and tea, while the evening hours are perfect for cocktails at the bar

43.menu: course menu, special full-course set menu, hanu gui (grilled Korean beef), glass wine pairing
43.desc: This Korean beef restaurant offers a luxurious dining experience with a stunning ocean view of Haeundae. Enjoy omakase (chef's choice) Korean beef dishes combining Japanese and French style. The restaurant has counter seats, several private rooms, and a large wine cellar.

44.desc: This Japanese restaurant located in the Centum Hotel offers high-quality sashimi. If you order a set menu, the sashimi is followed by a variety of seafood, vegetables and scallops, grilled beef, and then rice, soup, and side dishes. The sushi set menu is also popular, and the sake list is excellent too.

45.menu: lunch full-course set menu, dinner course
45.desc: This restaurant offers course set menus, which you can enjoy while taking in the view of the open sea. The course set menu consists of eight dishes, all of which is French cuisine with a Korean twist. The highlight of the meal is the steak, which is followed by a combination of Korean side dishes. The fish dishes included in the set menu change seasonally. Reservations are required.

46.menu: course menu, hanu bulgalbi (grilled marinated Korean beef), hanu yukhoe bibimbap (Korean beef tartare bibimbap), hanu tteokgalbi bansangcharim (grilled Korean galbi patties set menu)
46.desc: This long-standing Korean restaurant in the Westin Chosun Busan Hotel serves traditional Korean cuisine with sincerity. Its banquet hall, which has a view of Haeundae, is a popular place for important events.

47.menu: course menu, set, cheolpan course (griddled dish course)
47.desc: Located in Paradise Hotel, this Japanese restaurant serves authentic, high-quality cuisine made with fresh ingredients. The sushi counter is a popular choice, as is the teppanyaki, which highlights the natural flavors of the ingredients.

48.menu: course menu, hanu bulgogi bansang (bulgogi set menu)
48.desc: Located on the forty-third floor of Lotte Hotel Busan, this elegant Korean restaurant offers a panoramic view of Baekyang Mountain. They serve traditional cuisine for the nobility that has been reinterpreted as Korean set menus with a modern touch, making it popular with both Koreans and foreigners. The restaurant also has a wine list that pairs well with Korean food, as well as halal dishes for Muslims

49.desc: This restaurant offers a Japanese kaiseki dining experience with a view of Haeundae Beach. The authentic interior and staff's yukata (cotton kimono) create an immersive Japanese atmosphere. You can enjoy a wide range of dishes, from sashimi prepared with fresh seasonal ingredients, to suimono (broth), tempura, grilled dishes, and rice cooked in an iron pot. It is located on the second floor of Palé de Cz.

50.menu: full-course business set menu, Michael's course, salad, pasta, sandwich & burger, coconut shrimp, grilled calamari
50.desc: This American restaurant serves American-style dishes made with seasonal ingredients from Busan. Fajitas, truffle spaghetti, and Michael's signature burger are all recommended menu items. We highly recommend the outdoor terrace seats, which offer stunning night views of Busan. It is located in F1963, a multicultural complex.

51.desc: You can enjoy set menus and stunning night views in this modern Korean cuisine bar with a luxurious atmosphere. It serves set menus including a wide variety of seasonal seafood, such as octopus, eel, and yellowtail.

52.menu: lunch full-course set menu, dinner course
52.desc: LAB XXIV Kumuda is a high-end French restaurant run by Chef Edward Kwon. Enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of Songjeong Beach and refined full-course set menus at reasonable prices in a luxurious atmosphere. It is located on the fourth floor of the Kumuda Multiple Cultural Experience Space.

53.menu: jeomsim course (full-course lunch set menu) , chef's signature course , special full-course set menu , buldojang (Buddha's temptation soup), eojahaesamsongi (fried Korean sea cucumber and pine mushroom)
53.desc: Nampoong Chinese Restaurant has been a wellknown high-end Chinese restaurant in Busan for many years. It reinterprets traditional Cantonese Chinese cuisine in a Korean style. Their signature dishes include fried Korean sea cucumber, Cantonese veal ribs, and buldojang ('BuddhaJumps-Over-the-Wall' soup), all made with their own recipes. The restaurant is located on the third floor of the new building of Paradise Hotel, and offers stunning views of the ocean.

54.menu: dodari sekkosi (bone-in sliced raw ridged-eye flounder), ureok (rockfish), gwangeo (flatfish), jabeo (small fish), sea bream, gwangeo tongmari (whole flatfish)
54.desc: This restaurant is a great place to enjoy sekkosi (chopped raw small fish) while taking in the view of Gwangan Bridge. The secret of this restaurant's great-tasting food is the ssamjang (spicy soybean paste) that is served with the sekkosi. You can get high-quality sekkosi at a reasonable price, and the maeuntang (spicy seafood stew) made in an earthenware pot is also excellent.

55.menu: gomtang (beef bone soup), yanggomtang (beef tripe soup), teuk seokkeo gomtang (beef bone soup with beef tripe), suyuk (boiled pork slices)
55.desc: This restaurant specializes in gomtang, a light and refreshing soup made with Korean beef. Their yang-gomtang (beef soup with smooth tripe) is also a popular menu item. The terrace offers stunning views of Gwangan Bridge.

56.menu: galbitsal (grilled boneless galbi), deungsim (grilled sirloin), jebichuri (beef neck chain), kkotsal (grilled boneless short ribs)
56.desc: This restaurant specializes in Korean beef and offers great views of the sea. The Korean beef is high-quality and is grilled over charcoal, giving it a delicious flavor. If you order grilled Korean beef during lunchtime, rice and naengmyeon (cold noodles in chilled broth or spicy sauce) are included. The restaurant's exterior, which artfully blends water features and lawns, is so beautiful that it won an architectural award. There is also a café next door, which is a great place to enjoy a cup of tea after your meal.

57.menu: hanu deungsim (grilled Korean beef sirloin), hanu yangnyeom gui (grilled marinated Korean beef), hanu kkotdeungsim (Korean beef ribeye steak), yangnyeom galbitsal (grilled marinated boneless galbi), kkotgalbisal sogeumgui (grilled boneless galbi), hanu teuksubuwi modum (assorted special cuts of Korean beef), hanu kkotgalbisal (boneless Korean galbi), hanu gomtang (Korean beef bone soup), galbitang (galbi soup)
57.desc: At this restaurant specializing in charcoal-grilled beef ribs, you can enjoy Korean and imported beef. Take in the stunning views of Taejongdae as you dine. You can also enjoy a cup of tea at Café de Bom on the second floor, or make use of the banquet hall or outdoor wedding hall.

58.menu: afternoon tea set, black tea, herbal tea, gwasil cha (fruit tea), nokcha (green tea), jeontongcha (traditional Korean tea), espresso, Americano, cappuccino, caffe latte, caffe mocha, vanilla latte
58.desc: This lounge is located in the Ananti Hilton Busan. It is a place to enjoy dessert and tea while taking in the fantastic ocean view. The signature menu items are their baked goods, which include cakes, and the afternoon tea set with a selection of signature teas.

59.menu: vongole pasta (clam pasta), formaggi pasta, chaekkeut steak (striploin steaks), ansim steak (tenderloin steak), gamja twigim (french fries), lunch set, dinner set
59.desc: This steakhouse offers a stunning view of Gwangalli Sea and offers an à-la-carte menu. At lunch, a set menu is available that includes salad, pasta, Korean beef steak, and dessert. In the evening, it transforms into a wine bar.

60.menu: Geumnang hansang (raw fish full-course), Subyeon hansang, Gwangan hansang (raw fish full-course), Bada hansang, teuk modum hoe (assorted sliced raw fish special), modum hoe (assorted sliced raw fish)
60.desc: At this restaurant located in Gwangalli Waterside Park, you can enjoy a Korean table setting while taking in the views of Gwangan Bridge. They serve fresh sashimi, as well as plentiful side dishes including maeuntang (spicy fish stew), steamed abalone, mero (toothfish) steak, assorted seafood, and shrimp sauce. This restaurant was visited by former President Moon Jae-in.

61.menu: chaekkeut (striploin), ansim (grilled tenderloin), deungsim (grilled sirloin), kkotdeungsim (ribeye), teuk ansim (beef tenderloin), assorted grilled Korean beef cuts (rib-eye, tenderloin, brisket), omurice (rice-filled omelet)
61.desc: This restaurant specializes in grilled beef and offers a stunning view of the ocean. When you order meat, you will be served basic side dishes and three seasonings: salt, sesame oil, and demi-glace. The aged meat is flavorful, and the omurice with demiglace is also a satisfying meal on its own.

62.menu: hanu deungsim gui (grilled Korean beef sirloin), hanu ansim (Korean beef tenderloin), hanu tteokgalbi sotbap jeongsik (grilled Korean galbi patties with hot stone pot rice)
62.desc: This bungalow restaurant on the beach offers a stunning view and quality beef. A special feature is that it is dog-friendly. After your meal, it's nice to take a stroll along the beach.

63.menu: jayeonsan modum hoe (assorted sliced raw wild fish)
63.desc: This sashimi restaurant is located in Mipo, Haeundae. It is well known for its excellent wildcaught sashimi, as well as its various side dishes and maeuntang (spicy fish stew). The secret to the delicious taste is their chojang, a sauce made by mixing various seasonings with red pepper paste that has been aged for six months. This restaurant is a favorite of former President Moon Jae-in.

64.menu: kebab, pirzola (lamb chops), pita, lunch set, Cappadocia special (set menu including ekmek, lavash, and kebabs)
64.desc: This restaurant specializes in Turkish cuisine, which is rare in Busan. You can taste various authentic Turkish dishes, including kebabs. Various types of kebabs are popular, and the grilled pirzola (lamb ribs marinated in traditional spices) is also recommended. The restaurant is owned and operated by a Turkish immigrant, and traditional Turkish handicrafts are displayed throughout the store.

65.menu: poo pad pong curry (stir-fried crab and curry powder), poo nim pad pong curry (crispy fried soft-shell crab with curry powder), Thai sik haemul ssalguksu (Thai seafood rice noodles), pineapple bokkeumbap (pineapple fried rice), yum woon sen (Thai seafood and rice noodle salad), Aroi appetizer set menu
65.desc: This is a premium "Thai Select" restaurant, certified by the Thai government. You can savor authentic Thai cuisine prepared by a chef from a hotel in Thailand. Especially popular dishes are the poo pad pong curry, made with crab and fresh cream, and the fried rice with plenty of fresh pineapple.

66.menu: poo pad pong curry (stir-fried crab and curry powder), tom yum goong (hot and sour prawn soup),pad thai (Thai stir-fried rice noodles with meat and vegetables), green curry, red curry, som tam thai (Thai spicy green papaya salad), khao pad nea (beef fried rice), khao pad kung (shrimp fried rice), pat gra-prao moo sap (stir-fried minced pork), kao ka moo (braised pork trotters), quay tiew tom yum (tom yum noodle soup)
66.desc: This Thai restaurant's poo pad pong curry and tom yum goong are renowned. Here, you can enjoy authentic Thai cuisine. The food is even better when paired with Thai beer. The interior has been renovated and became modern and stylish.

67.menu: sogogi ssalguksu (beef rice noodles), Raeok pho ga (Raeok chicken pho), haemul bokkeumbap (seafood fried rice), banh xeo (crispy Vietnamese crêpes), goi cuon (cool shrimp, pork, or beef rice wraps), banh quay (fried breadstick), bunmangbit (Vietnamese duck vermicelli noodle soup), bun bo hue (spicy neef & pork noodle soup)
67.desc: The staff at this restaurant learned at Lai Ngọc, a rice noodle restaurant in Hanoi, Vietnam. They offer beef noodle soup with a clean-tasting broth. The bánh xèo is filled generously and also recommended. The interior, which recreates the atmosphere of the original restaurant, is also impressive.

68.desc: This restaurant offers French set menus that combine the chef's experience in France and Japan. The set menu changes seasonally according to what ingredients are locally available. The restaurant has a counter-style layout and is operated by a single chef, so reservations are essential. You can enjoy classic French dishes like escargot and rabbit at reasonable prices. There is also a diverse wine selection, so this is a good place for a glass of wine.

69.menu: crust pizza, ham cheese crust pizza, crust saeu pizza (shrimp pizza), pepperoni pizza, pasta
69.desc: This pizza place is a local favorite, known for its delicious cheese. Their pepperoni pizza is popular. You can upgrade your pizza to a larger size for an additional 4000 won. Be prepared to wait, as it can get busy.

70.menu: oyster, tongbal dansaeu (wild-caught sweet shrimp), Jeju san chamokdom (Jeju red tilefish), muneo risotto (octopus risotto), osso buco risotto, carbonara pasta, Itallia gajae pasta (Italian lobster pasta), bollonyasik sogogi pasta (bolognese pasta), hanu two plus chaekkeut steak (hanu strip loin steak)
70.desc: This is a great place to enjoy Italian cuisine and wine. The ddak-saewoo pasta, which harmonizes red-banded lobster from Jeju and linguine noodles, and the classic carbonara are popular dishes, and the osso buco risotto with tender veal is also highly recommended.

71.menu: aglio e olio pasta, cacio e pepe pasta, anchovy pasta, gorgonzola cheese pizza, prosciutto pizza, rucola pizza (arugula pizza), gambas al ajillo, maeun honghap jjim (spicy braised mussels), hanu chaekkeut (Korean beef strip loin)
71.desc: This Italian restaurant sticks to the basics, and the pasta dishes are the most popular items on the menu. The pizza is baked in an Italian woodfired oven, and you can taste the freshness of the ingredients. You can also enjoy Italian beer, which is not easily found elsewhere.

72.menu: salad, seonggeal eoran pasta (sea urchin & cured fish roe pasta), chorizo aglio e olio pasta, tomato ragu oven panne pasta, algamja gnocchi (baby potatoes gnocchi)
72.desc: This casual Italian restaurant is known for its delicious gnocchi. The potato-shaped gnocchi are perfectly paired with a rich truffle-and-cream sauce. The small garden in front of the entrance is a lovely touch.

73.menu: dinner course, saengmyeon pasta (fresh pasta), chaekkeut deungsim steak (striploin steaks)
73.desc: At this restaurant, you can enjoy high-quality Italian cuisine. It is known for its fresh pasta, which is made daily in-house. The wood-fired oven pizza and steak are also highly recommended. The set menu, which consists of a variety of dishes, is also very satisfying.

74.desc: This is a wine bar with a casual and lively atmosphere. Beef tartare, French-style minced raw beef, is a popular menu item and is served with baguette. Pasta is also available on the lunch menu. Liquor or soft drinks must be ordered with food.

75.desc: Here, they serve Japanese omakase (chef's choice) as a single course. Savor the genuine taste of the finest ingredients, such as fresh wasabi and sea urchin from Hokkaido. Various sake and tokuri (traditional sake flask) are also available to complement the dishes.

76.menu: yakitori omakase (chef's choice chicken skewers), chicken skewers, tsukune (japanese chicken meatball skewer), saengyachae boridoenjang (barley doenjang with fresh vegetables), chaeso gui (grilled vegetables), dak bong croquettes (chicken drumsticks croquettes), saeusisomari chungwon twigim (shrimp spring rolls with perilla leaves), cheese gui (grilled cheese)
76.desc: This yakitori restaurant with a lavish decor is renowned for its yakitori omakase (chef's choice chicken skewers) made with domestically-raised chickens. You can try almost every part of the chicken, including the tenderloin, neck, oyster, Achilles tendon, thigh, wing, leg, and skin.

77.desc: This sushi omakase (chef's choice) restaurant offers great value for the price. The shari (vinegared rice) made with akazu red vinegar pairs perfectly with rich-tasting fish like aji (horse mackerel) and saba (blue mackerel).

78.desc: This sushi restaurant offers sushi omakase (chef's choice) and is run by a solo chef. Dinner omakase is served in two sittings, only in the evening. Some people find the taste of the shari (vinegared rice) to be a bit strong, but others prefer it. Overall, the restaurant offers good value for the price.

79.desc: Here, you can enjoy Japanese kaiseki (multicourse set menu). They use seasonal, high-quality ingredients, including geumtae (blackthroat seaperch), tuna, sea urchin roe, sweet shrimp, and beef. The meal is served in small portions, allowing you to try a variety of dishes, including sashimi, suimono (broth), soba (buckwheat noodles), grilled dishes, and rice cooked in an iron pot.

80.menu: otsumami (finger foods) set menu, potato salad, dashimaki tamago (rolled omelet), tataki kyuuri (smashed cucumber salad), oshinko moriawase (assorted Japanese pickled vegetables), daikon sarada (radish salad), negi toro maki (sushi diced tuna with green onion), sunagimo (gizzard), nankotsu (chicken cartilage), seseri (grilled chicken neck), tebasaki (deep-fried chicken wings), momo (dumplings), udon, soba (Japanese buckwheat noodles)
80.desc: This is a great place to have a drink along with the set menu of otsumami (Izakaya-style side dishes). You can also order à la carte and choose from a wide variety of skewers and Japanese snacks. This branch in Busan was opened by Chef Yokomori, who is also the owner of Mozu, a popular restaurant in Sinsa-dong, Seoul.

81.menu: donggyeongsik minmul jangeo deopbap (Tokyo-style stirfried eel with rice (unaju)) , nagoyasik minmul jangeo deopbap (Nagoya style stir-fried eel with rice (hitsumabushi)), minmul jangeo deopbap (stir-fried eel with rice)
81.desc: This restaurant specializes in rice topped with grilled eel, which are available in Tokyo-style unaju and Nagoya-style hitsumabushi. After eating some of the rice and eel, you can finish it as ochazuke (green tea over rice), which is characteristic of hitsumabshi

82.menu: wonton soup, gogi mandu (meat mandu), kimchi mandu, mul mandu (boiled mandu), samsaek modum mandu (tricolor mandu), gajiyori (eggplant), tomato gyeran bokkeum (stir-fried tomato and egg), ohyang jangyuk (five-spice pork), mapa dubu (spicy bean curd)
82.desc: This is a place where you can enjoy wontons and dumplings at a reasonable price, and you can experience the flavors of mainland China. The dishes and anju (side dishes for drinking) arereasonably priced, making it an excellent place for a drink. The mapo tofu (tofu and minced meat in a spicy sauce) and eggplant dishes are highly recommended.

83.menu: sacheonsik baechujjim (Sichuan braised napa cabbage), chashu, maui sangsu (spicy fried cellophane noodles and ground pork), sannibaegyuk (garlic pork on a bed of thin-sliced cucumber), dim sum, Peking duck, lunch set, dinner set
83.desc: This modern Chinese restaurant is decorated black tones. The signature dish is Peking duck with crispy skin, made properly in a dedicated wood-fired oven. They also serve a variety of familiar Chinese dishes with a modern twist. Two unique dishes that are noteworthy are their ma-yi-shang-shu (spicy fried cellophane noodles and ground pork) and suan-nibai-rou (pork with spicy garlic sauce).

84.menu: jjajangmyeon (noodles in black bean sauce), jjamppong (spicy seafood noodle soup), junghwa deopbap (chinese bibimbap), sacheon laziji (Sichuan spicy stir-fried chicken), yuringi (deep-fried chicken in hot and sour soy sauce), gungbogijeong (kung pao chicken), menbosha (fried shrimp sandwich), tangsuyuk (deep-fried pork with sweet and sour sauce)
84.desc: This Chinese restaurant is a popular spot in Busan. You can enjoy great Chinese food at a reasonable price. One outstanding item on the menu is the Sichuan laziji (mala chicken), which features a harmonious blend of spicy flavors and ingredients. All dishes come topped with a fried egg.

85.menu: ttalgi mille-feuille (strawberry mille-feuille), tarte chocolat, orange cocoa madeleine, muhwagwa keurimchijeu financier (fig butter cream cheese financier), Haenam bamgoguma crème brulée (sweet potato crème brulée), Americano, caffe latte
85.desc: This abalone restaurant offers a luxurious dining experience. The basic set includes abalone rice, abalone porridge, and grilled abalone. You can choose between miyeok (seaweed), hijiki seaweed, and gondre (Korean thistle) as a garnish for the abalone rice and mix in some gewoo sauce (a sauce made with abalone innards) and abalone paste.

86.menu: bungjangeo hoe (sliced raw conger eel), modum hoe (assorted sliced raw fish), dodari (ridged-eye flounder), chamgajami (flouder), dom (sea bream), maeuntang (spicy fish stew)
86.desc: This is a long-standing restaurant that serves anago (conger eel). Try the dried anago sashimi, which is best enjoyed dipped in makjang (fermented soybean-and-barley sauce). The spicy maeuntang (spicy fish soup) that comes with the anago sashimi is also tasty. The restaurant is located in a scenic spot overlooking the sea and offers stunning views.

87.menu: samgyeop loseu (grilled pork belly), samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), moksal (grilled pork shoulder), yangnyeom samgyeomn loseu (grilled marinated pork belly), hangjeongsal (grilled pork neck), mul naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles), bibim naengmyeon (spicy buckwheat noodles), chadol doenjang (beef brisket soybean paste jjigae)
87.desc: This restaurant offers a variety of high-quality grilled beef and pork. The meat is grilled to perfection for you, so you can enjoy your meal without any hassle. Seasoned green onions and mel-jeot (salted anchovies) are also served with the meat, and make for a delicious combination. A popular dish is mul-naengmyeon, noodles in a chilled, savory broth with a meaty flavor.

88.menu: daegutang (codfish soup), daegu ppoljjim (braised codfish head)
88.desc: Here, the popular dish is daegu-tang, a cod soup with a refreshing broth. It is characterized by the addition of cod heads to give the soup flavor. The side dishes, which include various jangajji (pickled side dishes) and mungae-jeot (salted sea squirts), are delicious. The restaurant is also a favorite of artist Heo Young-man and celebrity Jeong Woo.

89.menu: soonmemil naengmyeons (cold buckwheat noodles), sari (side order), matbogi hanu suyuk (Korean beef suyuk taster), hanu hanmari kkorisuyuk (boiled Korean oxtail slices), kkori gomtang (oxtail and beef bone soup), yukgaejang (spicy beef soup)
89.desc: This restaurant specializes in Pyongyang-style naengmyeon, which are noodles served in a chilled, clean-tasting broth. They normally offer only two dishes: Pyongyang naengmyeon and suyuk (steamed pork), but in winter, they also serve gomtang (ox bone soup) and yukgaejang (spicy beef stew).

90.menu: hanu yangnyeom galbi (grilled marinated Korean galbi), ansim (grilled tenderloin), galbitsal (grilled boneless galbi), deungsim (grilled sirloin), anchangsal (grilled thin skirt), Pyeongyang naengmyeon (pyeongyang cold buckwheat noodles), gomtang (beef bone soup), jeomsim teukseon (lunch special)
90.desc: This restaurant offers high-quality 1++ grade Korean beef in a luxurious setting. Their specialty is yangnyeom-galbi (marinated short ribs), but they also serve a variety of other cuts, such as short ribs, eye filet, and outside skirt. The regular side dishes are usually tasty, and the Pyongyang naengmyeon is great for refreshing your palate.

91.menu: kkeopdegi (pork rinds), sogeum gui (salt-grilledmeat), dwaeji galbi (grilled pork galbi), dwitgogi (various pork cuts), daepae samgyeopsal (grilled thin-sliced pork belly), tongsamgyeop kimchi jjigae (pork and kimchi jjigae)
91.desc: This is a popular grilled pork restaurant in Haeundae. Its flavorful, chewy meat pairs well with the green onions and sauce. The signature dish is the honeycomb-cut pork rinds. They offer a very satisfying meal for the price.

92.menu: jayeonsan hoe (sliced raw wild fish), isigari(roughscale sole)
92.desc: Here, you can enjoy ishigari (roughscale sole) sashimi, which is known for its savory, fatty flavor. Other wild-caught fish are also available, so you can enjoy sashimi of various high-quality fish such as domi (sea bream) and gajami (sole). Enjoy the rich-flavored maeuntang (spicy fish soup), which is served afterward.

93.menu: jeomsim teukseon hoe jeongsik (lunch special sliced raw fish set), hoe course (sliced raw fish full-course set menu), sekkosi (bone-in sliced raw fish)
93.desc: This wild-caught sashimi restaurant is a local favorite because their fish is so fresh. When you order sashimi, you are also served a variety of seafood and tempura. In Busan, it is customary to dip sashimi in ssamjang (soybean paste), and you can make sushi by placing sashimi on sushi rice. They serve maeuntang (spicy fish soup) and steamed fish as part of your meal.

94.menu: galchi gui (braised cutlassfish), galchi jjigae (cutlassfishjjigae), galchi jorim(braised cutlassfish)
94.desc: This restaurant specializes in fresh Jeju kalchi(hairtail) dishes. When you order extra-large grilled kalchi, the pieces are thick and the size of your hand, and have an exquisite texture that is firm and tender. The kalchi-jjigae (hairtail stew) with a doenjang (soybean paste) base has a light and refreshingly spicy taste and is also popular. The side dishes, along with three kinds of salted fish, that they serve are also delicious and neat.

95.menu: Eonyang bulgogi, deungsim (grilled sirloin), saeng galbitsal (grilled boneless galbi), yuk sashimi (sliced raw beef)
95.desc: This restaurant specializes in Eonyang-style bulgogi, which is made with thinly sliced highquality beef that is marinated in a unique Eonyang seasoning and then grilled over charcoal. The taste is exquisite, and it is best enjoyed wrapped in the white kimchi that is served with it.

96.desc: This meat restaurant offers two dishes: thinly sliced pork belly and seasoned pork ribs. It also serves a variety of side dishes that go well with the meat, as well as sikhye (sweet rice punch) for dessert. The seasoned crab is a popular side dish. This is a place where you can enjoy a meal at an affordable price.

97.menu: dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), naejang gukbap (offal and rice soup), suyuk baekban (boiled pork slices set menu), dwaeji suyuk (boiled pork slices), naejang suyuk (boiled offal slices)
97.desc: This restaurant specializes in dwaeji-gukbap(pork soup with rice) and is so popular that there is often a line out the door. Rice is placed in an earthenware pot, and then the soup is poured over it and removed multiple times before serving. The soup is best enjoyed by adding plenty of jeongguji(seasoned Chinese chives). The suyuk (boiled pork) made with hanjoengsal (pork jowl) is also recommended.

98.menu: son kalguksu (handmade noodle soup), bibim sonkalguksu(spicy handmade noodles), naeng kalguksu (cold handmade noodle soup), gimbap
98.desc: This restaurant specializes in Gyeongsang-do style kalguksu (handmade noodle soup), served in anchovy broth and topped with crown daisy and Chinese chives. It is light and refreshing, with a hint of sesame seeds and minced garlic. The noodles are made by rolling out the dough, and the only side dish is kkakdugi (radish kimchi). The dish is simple, but generously portioned, with a homemade taste.

99.menu: ttaro gukbap (rice and soup), suyuk baekban (boiled pork slices set menu), suyuk (boiled pork slices), modum suyuk (assorted boiled pork slices), sundae (Korean sausage)
99.desc: This restaurant serves dwaeji-gukbap (pork soup with rice) that has a clear broth. When you order dwaeji-gukbap, the broth is poured over pork innards, such as intestines and uterus, several times before serving. Different variations of gukbap are available, all with rice on the side: modeum ddaro (with assorted meat (pork, sundae, and pork intestines)); sundae ddaro (with Korean sausage); naejang ddaro (with pork intestines); or ddaro (with only pork). It is best enjoyed with plenty of chives as is the custom in Busan.

100.menu: yangnyeom galbi (grilled marinated galbi), dwaeji moksal (grilled pork shoulder), saeng galbi (grilled galbi), samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), doenjang jjigae (soybean paste jjigae)
100.desc: At this restaurant, you can have dwaeji-galbi (porkshort ribs), moksal (pork neck), and samgyeopsal(pork belly). It is neither big nor fancy; however, the side dishes and meat are delicious, so it's always full of customers. The pork ribs marinated in homemade seasoning are the most popular dish on the menu.
